hints: Start by naming the type of pathogen for each disease: what kind of organism causes HIV/AIDS, what kind causes malaria, and what kind causes TB?
Remember which structures need a true cell to exist, and which one every pathogen must have to carry instructions for making new copies of itself.
walkthrough:
**Identify the three pathogens**

Great first move is to sort out who is who. HIV is caused by a virus. Malaria is caused by Plasmodium, which is a eukaryotic protoctist. TB is caused by Mycobacterium, which is a prokaryotic bacterium.

So we are comparing a non-cellular virus, a eukaryotic cell and a prokaryotic cell.

**Check cell surface membrane and ribosomes**

Both malaria and TB pathogens are true cells, so they both have a cell surface membrane and ribosomes for protein synthesis.

HIV as a virus is not a cell. It has no cell surface membrane and no ribosomes of its own, it uses the host cell machinery instead. So these two features are not common to all three.

**Check genes**

Every pathogen must be able to store and pass on instructions to make more of itself. HIV stores this as RNA genes, while Plasmodium and Mycobacterium store this as DNA genes.

Different chemical, same idea. Genes are common to all three, so the pattern is no, yes, no, which is option D.

options.A: Incorrect, because HIV has no cell surface membrane and no ribosomes, so all three features cannot be common.
options.B: Incorrect, because genes are common to all three, and ribosomes are missing from HIV, so this combination is backwards.
options.C: Incorrect, because although genes are correctly included, ribosomes are not present in the HIV virus.
options.D: Correct, because only genes are shared by virus, bacterium and protoctist, while cell surface membrane and ribosomes are absent from HIV.
